hashConvention: SHA-256 of UTF-8 LF-normalized source text and exact Pester It AST extents

selectors.selector: chooses a complete toolkit supporting every requested code target
selectors.reviewScope: Reproduces the prior refusal of realistic numeric-only nvcc output. Pins both a/f support to assembler output from the same eligible toolkit and skips the incompatible toolkit assembler.

selectors.selector: rejects a generic Blackwell toolkit for an architecture-specific target
selectors.reviewScope: An explicit sm_120a request still fails when ptxas advertises only sm_120f, even if nvcc lists sm_120a.

selectors.selector: keeps candidate order when no target architecture is requested
rejects a malformed target list before probing nvcc
prioritizes the selected CUDA bin already present in PATH
selectors.reviewScope: The exact bootstrap assignment deduplicates the selected bin, keeps unrelated segments, and inserts bin/x64 directly after bin when the directory first appears.

selectors.selector: requires the same toolkit ptxas only for suffixed targets
selectors.reviewScope: A numeric request succeeds without ptxas. A suffixed request fails closed and no assembler invocation occurs for either case.

selectors.selector: reads exact suffixed code names from wrapped assembler help
selectors.reviewScope: The real Gen7 CUDA 13.1 GPU-name allowed-values list inserts LTO entries between compute and SM entries. The fixture reproduced an empty result on aa4aaee0, verifies that other option entries are excluded, and certifies only exact SM suffixes. The read-only Gen7 retest selected sm_89, sm_120, sm_120a and sm_120f.

selectors.selector: probes the effective CUDA declaration for <Case>
selectors.protects: Each backend validates its effective CUDA declaration, including a numeric legacy GGML override when shell defaults request unsupported targets.
selectors.detects: An unrelated default rejecting a valid backend, a missing effective declaration, or a combined backend build checking only one target list.
selectors.needs: Pester 5, the actual extracted CUDA branch, inert directories and a synthetic nvcc code list.
selectors.reviewScope: Baseline daff6198 failed four of six cases. The revised branch and real toolkit selector use each effective declaration without invoking nvcc or a real CUDA install.

selectors.selector: rejects an architecture suffix in legacy GGML input <Target>
selectors.protects: Legacy GGML receives numeric architecture targets only.
selectors.detects: A suffixed target, including a dotted target, reaching the compiler and later being discarded.
selectors.needs: Pester 5, the extracted production CUDA branch, a stub that throws if invoked.
selectors.reviewScope: Both compact and dotted suffix spellings fail before a compiler probe.

selectors.selector: preserves the GGML override and compiler after optional CUDA library setup
selectors.protects: The child receives the admitted GGML target and selected CUDA compiler and runtime directories after optional library setup.
selectors.detects: Dropping the target export, leaving the CUDA 13 runtime directory behind optional directories, or removing unrelated prior entries.
selectors.needs: Pester 5, TestDrive, the extracted production CUDA branch and actual path helper with inert discovery and library stubs.
selectors.reviewScope: The actual CUDA recipe reasserts bin and bin/x64 after cuDNN and TensorRT each prepend. Both optional paths and the prior unrelated path still resolve in order.

selectors.protects: Native compiler and assembler exit status and output jointly determine whether the candidate is admitted.
selectors.detects: Trusting stdout from a nonzero command and mistaking successful empty compiler output for unsupported code.
selectors.needs: Windows cmd.exe, Pester TestDrive, and actual CUDA probe function bodies. The selector sees inert .exe markers while each real probe spawns a .cmd fixture.
selectors.reviewScope: At 3128c32e the three production controls passed. Removing either tool exit guard admits its valid-looking failing stub, and bypassing the empty nvcc guard changes the rejection reason for both invalid nvcc outputs. These three source mutations were rejected.

selectors.selector: hands Mistral the admitted architecture for <Case>
selectors.protects: The selected toolkit can compile the actual explicitly declared Mistral kernel target.
selectors.detects: Losing an explicit declaration, accepting Blackwell without the assembler target cudaforge uses, or changing automatic detection.
selectors.needs: Pester 5, the extracted production CUDA branch, the actual selector and inert compiler and assembler advertisements.
selectors.reviewScope: Seven red cases on the runtime-path change alone turn green. Two controls keep auto and multi-value fallback unchanged. This fixture qualifies argument selection only.

selectors.selector: leaves a foreign CUDA runtime in place when the selected toolkit has none
selectors.protects: The selected compiler stays first while unrelated PATH entries retain their order.
selectors.detects: Promoting a foreign runtime when the selected toolkit has no bin/x64 directory.
selectors.needs: Pester TestDrive, two inert toolkit directories and a process-scoped PATH.
selectors.reviewScope: The selector fails when the helper takes a foreign bin/x64 directory from PATH. The production helper passes.

selectors.selector: restores the inherited Mistral CUDA target after <Case>
selectors.protects: The original Mistral CUDA target is restored for the next build in the same process.
selectors.detects: A build-specific CUDA target surviving success or a terminating build error.
selectors.needs: Pester, the actual top-level build tail and inert initialization, build and artifact copy.
selectors.reviewScope: All four cases fail when the actual restoration assignment is removed. The production tail passes with and without an inherited target.
